items.claim: Deliver or drop the promised data-focused unlatch. The description says a control that unmounts or becomes disabled while focused no longer latches `data-focused`, but the diff adds no such code: at head `setFocused(false)` is still reached only from `onBlur`, the relocated `autoFocus` effect has no cleanup, and `FieldRoot` never resets `focused` on `disabled`.
items.consequence: When a focused control is conditionally unmounted or disabled, no blur fires, so `Field.Root`, `Field.Label`, and `Field.Description` keep `data-focused` and focused styling, the bug the description claims is fixed.
items.proposed_fix: Either clear the focused state in `FieldControl.tsx` with a layout-effect cleanup on unmount and when `disabled` turns true while the control is the active element, adding a test for each path, or remove the claim from the description.

items.claim: Is the Field.Validity value type change for non-string controlled values an accepted break?
items.consequence: If maintainers treat the type of these public fields as part of the released contract, the change needs a breaking-change note or a raw-value baseline kept alongside the serialized comparison; if not, nothing further is owed. Status is already Changes Requested, so the answer affects release notes rather than this merge decision.
items.proposed_fix: A Base UI maintainer decides whether `Field.Validity.State.value`/`initialValue` and the submit-time `validate` argument for non-string controlled `Field.Control` values are contractually raw; yes reopens this id as a compatibility finding, no closes it.

items.claim: The description's `processedValueRef` guard is not in the code; the head returns early from `onChange` for controlled inputs and routes every controlled update through `useValueChanged(serializedValue, ...)`, which the new once-per-keystroke validation test covers.
items.consequence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:105-115`, `:142-146`; `FieldControl.test.tsx` "validates once when a controlled value is changed by the user".

items.claim: The description says this PR does not call `clearErrors(name)` on value changes, but the head calls it on every controlled value change, so the body's open question is already resolved toward the sibling controls.
items.consequence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:110`; pr-body "This PR does not, so a programmatic change clears a server error on a Switch but not on an Input."

items.claim: The mount effect no longer clears `filled` for an empty controlled value, so a control remounted with `value=""` under a persisting, already-filled `Field.Root` keeps `data-filled` where the merge-base cleared it; later value changes still update it through `useValueChanged`.
